What the Academy Is

From your first XR scene
to a live LBXR prototype.

The IMMENSIVA XR Academy is a 9-week online programme for individual creators, developers and practitioners moving into immersive XR production. The curriculum moves in a deliberate arc: beginning with practical XR basics and hands-on STYLY production, deepening into theory and creative development, and culminating in a full Location-Based XR prototype.

The Academy is designed for individuals. Each participant develops their own project throughout the programme. The cohort provides peer community, structured feedback and a shared production environment — but every prototype is a single practitioner's work.

Completers receive a verifiable Espronceda professional micro-credential — a short, stackable, outcome-based qualification aligned with European Micro-Credentials standards.

Programme Arc

Nine weeks.
One continuous arc.

The programme builds deliberately — tool literacy first, then theory, then full production, then showcase. Each phase depends on the one before it.

Phase 01
XR Basics
WEEKS 1–3 · HARDWARE / PLATFORMS / STYLY FUNDAMENTALS / FORMAT LANDSCAPE
01
WEEK 01
Welcome to XR — Hardware, Platforms & Your First Experience
Get hands-on immediately. Understand the hardware landscape, set up your tools, and build your first spatial scene.
+
Session Overview

The first session is deliberately practical. Rather than beginning with theory, participants get hands-on with XR hardware and platforms from the very first hour. We cover the current hardware landscape — headsets, tethered vs standalone, 3DoF vs 6DoF — and move straight into platform setup. By the end of Week 1 every participant has a STYLY account, has navigated a published spatial experience, and has placed their first object in a scene.

FormatLive online · 3 hours · recorded
DeliverablePublished first spatial scene in STYLY
Note: Participants should have a VR headset or access to one. WebXR preview in browser available for those without.
Topics Covered
  • The XR hardware landscape: VR, AR and MR headsets — what exists, what they can do, what they cost
  • 3DoF vs 6DoF: degrees of freedom and what they mean for creators
  • Standalone vs tethered: Meta Quest, PICO, HTC Vive, Apple Vision Pro — a practical comparison
  • Platform overview: STYLY, Unity, Unreal, WebXR — where does each fit?
  • Setting up STYLY: account, editor, spatial publishing workflow
  • Navigating a published STYLY experience from the inside
  • Your first spatial scene: placing objects, setting scale, publishing to headset
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
STYLY account set up and editor navigated
[ ✓ ]
First spatial scene built and published
[ ✓ ]
Hardware landscape understood
02
WEEK 02
Building in STYLY — Assets, Audio, Interaction & Publishing
Go deeper into STYLY's production tools — importing assets, spatial audio, basic interactions and a complete mini-experience.
+
Session Overview

Building on the first scene from Week 1, this session goes deeper into STYLY's core production toolkit. Participants learn to import and manage 3D assets, integrate spatial audio, build basic interactive elements using STYLY's visual scripting system, and publish a complete mini-experience. The session establishes the production workflow that carries through the rest of the programme.

FormatLive online workshop · 3 hours · recorded
DeliverablePublished mini-experience with assets, audio + interaction
Note: Bring your Week 1 scene. The mini-experience produced here becomes the technical foundation for your Phase 2 prototype.
Topics Covered
  • Asset types in STYLY: 3D models, images, video, audio, particle systems
  • Importing and managing assets: file formats, scale, optimisation basics
  • Spatial audio in STYLY: 3D sound placement, ambience, proximity triggers
  • STYLY visual scripting: building basic interactions without code
  • Proximity events, gaze triggers and controller inputs
  • Scene optimisation: performance, draw calls, poly count
  • Publishing workflow: from editor to headset to public URL
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Import and place 3D assets in a STYLY scene
[ ✓ ]
Add spatial audio to your scene
[ ✓ ]
Publish a complete mini-experience with at least one interaction
03
WEEK 03
XR Formats & Use Cases — VR, AR, MR and Location-Based XR
Understand the full spectrum of XR formats, their distinct affordances, and where Location-Based XR fits in the landscape.
+
Session Overview

With hands-on STYLY experience established, this session steps back to map the full XR format landscape — not as abstract categories but as distinct creative and spatial possibilities. Particular focus is given to Location-Based XR (LBXR): what it is, why it matters for cultural and artistic production, how it differs from home VR, and what it demands of creators. Participants leave with a clear format decision for their own project.

FormatLive online · 2.5 hours · recorded
DeliverableFormat decision document (1 page)
Note: By the end of this session every participant should have a clear format decision. This decision shapes the entire production phase.
Topics Covered
  • VR, AR, MR: definitions, distinctions and creative affordances
  • Location-Based XR: definition, history, current landscape and key venues
  • How LBXR differs from home VR: space, scale, mediation, audience, social experience
  • STYLY and LBXR: how the platform supports location-based deployment
  • Use cases across sectors: culture, heritage, education, entertainment, activism
  • Case studies: NewImages, Cannes Immersive, Venice Gap
  • Choosing your format: matching your concept to the right XR modality
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Understand the full XR format spectrum
[ ✓ ]
Articulate what LBXR is and why it matters
[ ✓ ]
Identify which XR format fits your project concept
Phase 02
Theory & Creative Development
WEEKS 4–6 · SPATIAL STORYTELLING / PRESENCE / EMBODIMENT / INTERACTION DESIGN
04
WEEK 04
Spatial Storytelling & Narrative Design for Immersive Experience
How stories work when the audience moves through them — narrative design for non-linear, embodied, location-triggered space.
+
Session Overview

The first theory session makes the shift from tool-literacy to creative thinking. Participants learn the principles of spatial storytelling — how narrative works differently when the audience is embodied within it, when sequence is non-linear, when the environment itself is the story. The session draws on examples from theatre, game design, architecture and XR. Participants draft their first spatial narrative outline for their own project.

FormatLive online · 2.5 hours · recorded
DeliverableSpatial narrative outline (1–2 pages)
Note: Joint session with IMMENSIVA residency teams — direct contact with practitioners building professional LBXR works right now.
Topics Covered
  • What makes immersive narrative different: embodiment, agency, non-linearity, presence
  • The grammar of spatial storytelling: scene, threshold, encounter, revelation, loop
  • Designing for movement: how participant motion becomes narrative progression
  • Non-linear structures: branching, layered, ambient, episodic
  • Location as dramaturgy: how space carries meaning in LBXR
  • Examples from XR, theatre, installation art and game design
  • Drafting a spatial narrative outline for your project
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Understand spatial narrative principles
[ ✓ ]
Draft a spatial narrative outline for your project
[ ✓ ]
Connect your format choice to your narrative structure
05
WEEK 05
Presence, Embodiment & the Neuroscience of Immersive Experience
What the body believes — the science and design of felt presence, spatial audio, environmental design and sensory layering.
+
Session Overview

The most powerful quality of XR is not visual fidelity — it is presence: the feeling of actually being somewhere. This session goes deep into the neuroscience and design principles of presence, covering what the body responds to, how spatial audio is the single most powerful presence driver, and how environmental design, pacing and sensory layering combine to produce genuine felt experience. Participants apply these principles directly to their project concept.

FormatLive online · 2.5 hours · recorded
DeliverableUpdated STYLY scene with spatial audio + presence notes
Topics Covered
  • The neuroscience of presence: what the body believes vs what the eyes see
  • Embodiment in XR: avatar, body ownership illusion, the rubber hand experiment
  • Spatial audio as the primary presence driver: implementation in STYLY
  • Environmental design: scale, light, texture, breath and rhythm
  • Sensory layering without cognitive overload
  • Pacing and tempo: when to hold, when to release, when to overwhelm
  • Applying 3 presence techniques to your own project concept
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Understand the neuroscience of presence
[ ✓ ]
Apply 3 presence techniques to your project
[ ✓ ]
Implement spatial audio in your STYLY scene
06
WEEK 06
Milestone Review 01
Interaction Design & UX for LBXR
Body-centred interaction, accessibility-first design, and building the user journey for location-based immersive experience.
+
Session Overview

This session focuses on how people actually move through, touch and make meaning within LBXR environments. Participants learn UX principles specific to location-based immersive work — from spatial onboarding and body-centred interaction to accessibility-first design and the specific safety requirements of LBXR. The session covers STYLY's interaction tools in depth and moves into structured user journey mapping for each participant's project.

FormatLive online workshop · 3 hours · recorded
DeliverableUser journey map + 3 interaction moments in STYLY
Milestone Review #1 — structured peer and facilitator feedback on current prototype state at the end of this session.
Topics Covered
  • UX principles for LBXR: affordance, feedback, flow, safety and recovery
  • Body-centred interaction: movement, gaze, gesture, proximity and physical props
  • Spatial onboarding: bringing an audience into LBXR safely and clearly
  • Accessibility-first design: motion sensitivity, cognitive load, physical access
  • STYLY interaction tools in depth: visual scripting, proximity events, multi-user sync
  • User journey mapping across physical and digital layers
  • Designing 3 core interaction moments for your project
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Map your full user journey for LBXR
[ ✓ ]
Design 3 core interaction moments in STYLY
[ ✓ ]
Document your accessibility plan
Phase 03
LBXR Production with STYLY
WEEKS 7–8 · PROTOTYPE BUILD / MULTI-USER / SPATIAL ANCHORING / ETHICS / STRATEGY
07
WEEK 07
Building Your LBXR Prototype in STYLY
From concept to working prototype — advanced STYLY production, multi-user configuration, spatial anchoring and venue simulation.
+
Session Overview

The production phase begins in earnest. This session moves participants from conceptual development into full prototype build, using STYLY's advanced production tools. The focus is on the specific requirements of LBXR: multi-user configuration, spatial anchoring, venue geometry simulation, and the physical-digital integration that defines location-based work. Each participant leaves with a working prototype — fully navigable and demonstrating their core concept.

FormatLive online workshop · 3 hours · recorded
DeliverableWorking LBXR prototype in STYLY (link + docs)
Note: The most technically intensive session. Identify your blockers the week prior. Facilitator async support extended this week.
Topics Covered
  • STYLY advanced production: layered scenes, conditional logic, state management
  • Multi-user configuration: shared spatial experiences and synchronisation
  • Spatial anchoring: locking digital content to physical space
  • Venue geometry simulation: building a physical space into your scene for testing
  • Physical-digital integration: props, markers, spatial triggers
  • Performance optimisation for LBXR deployment
  • Prototype review process: documenting decisions, logging blockers, iterating
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Working LBXR prototype in STYLY
[ ✓ ]
Multi-user or spatial anchoring implemented
[ ✓ ]
Prototype documented and ready for peer review
08
WEEK 08
Milestone Review 02
Ethics, Sustainability & Going Professional
Responsible LBXR practice, environmental cost, funding models, distribution and positioning your work for the international market.
+
Session Overview

The penultimate session combines two essential threads: the ethical and environmental responsibilities of immersive practice, and the professional strategy for taking a finished prototype into the world. The first half covers ethics, consent, data, accessibility and sustainability in LBXR. The second half covers the full landscape of XR funding, distribution and international positioning — from EU grants and festival circuits to institutional markets and commercial LBXR venues.

FormatLive online · 3 hours · recorded
DeliverableEthics audit + draft pitch deck + 3 pathways
Milestone Review #2 — prototype progress reviewed before the final sprint. Joint session with IMMENSIVA residency teams.
Topics Covered
  • Ethics in LBXR: data, consent, surveillance, representation and positionality
  • Environmental cost of immersive tech: hardware, compute, carbon footprint
  • Accessibility in LBXR: motion sensitivity, physical access, inclusive design
  • Completing the ethics audit: a structured rubric for your prototype
  • Funding landscape: EU Creative Europe, arts councils, foundations, co-production
  • Distribution: Tribeca, NewImages, Cannes Immersive, SXSW, institutional touring
  • Pitch deck structure: artist statement, technical rider, media pack, positioning
Learning Outcomes
[ ✓ ]
Complete your ethics audit
[ ✓ ]
Draft your project pitch deck
[ ✓ ]

Phase 04
Showcase
WEEK 9 · PROTOTYPE SPRINT / PEER CRITIQUE / PORTFOLIO / FINAL ONLINE SHOWCASE
09
WEEK 09
Prototype Sprint, Peer Review & Final Online Showcase
Intensive capstone sprint, structured peer critique, portfolio brief and final showcase with the IMMENSIVA/NubiaLabs network.
+
Session Overview

The final week is the culmination of the entire programme. Participants complete their LBXR prototypes in an intensive sprint, go through structured peer critique using a shared rubric, prepare their portfolio brief and presentation materials, and present in the final online showcase. The showcase is attended by invited practitioners from the IMMENSIVA and NubiaLabs networks. Participants who complete all deliverables and present receive the Espronceda professional micro-credential.

FormatIntensive sprint + live online showcase · Full day
DeliverablePrototype + portfolio brief + showcase presentation
Note: The showcase is public. Exceptional work may be invited to apply for the IMMENSIVA Residency or NubiaLabs incubation track.
Topics Covered
  • Capstone prototype sprint: final production push in STYLY
  • Portfolio brief: documenting your project for professional audiences
  • Pitch preparation: live demonstration format, spoken introduction and Q&A
  • Structured peer critique using the shared rubric
  • Final online showcase: live demos with the IMMENSIVA/NubiaLabs network
  • Credential completion: requirements, verification, what the statement means
  • Next steps: IMMENSIVA Residency, NubiaLabs incubation, independent production
